title: The blue jackal.
lines: This is an old story from India.
It comes from a book of animal stories, the Panchatantra.
Long ago a jackal lived in a big forest.
A jackal looks a bit like a fox and a bit like a dog.
This jackal's name was Chandu.
One evening Chandu was very hungry.
There was nothing left to eat in the forest.
Then I'll go to the village, he thought.
Maybe I'll find something tasty there.
He crept into the village.
It was dark.
But the village dogs smelled him straight away.
Woof, woof, woof!
They barked and they ran after him.
Chandu ran as fast as he could.
He ran through the streets, past the houses and across a courtyard.
And splash!
He fell into a big barrel full of blue dye.
The dye belonged to the man who coloured fabrics.
Chandu climbed out of the barrel.
The dogs were gone.
They couldn't smell him anymore because of the dye.
Chandu walked back to the forest.
The next morning he looked into the water of the river.
What did he see?
He was completely blue!
Blue ears, a blue nose, a blue tail.
Oh dear, he thought.
But then Chandu had an idea.
A clever idea, he thought.
He stood in the middle of the forest.
The other animals came to look.
The hare, the deer, the monkey, the elephant, and even the lion and the tiger.
What kind of animal is that?
they whispered.
We've never seen such a blue animal before!
Chandu puffed out his chest.
I am a special animal, he said.
The sky has sent me.
I am your new king!
The animals were impressed.
They bowed to the blue king.
From that day on they had to bring him the tastiest food every day.
Mangoes, bananas, honey.
Chandu lay in the shade all day and did nothing.
And do you know what else he did?
He sent all the other jackals away from the forest.
Because he was afraid they would recognise him.
And so Chandu lived like a king for a while.
But one evening, when the moon came up, he heard a sound in the distance.
It was the other jackals.
They were howling at the moon, the way jackals do.
Owoooo!
Owoooo!
And Chandu?
He couldn't help himself.
It was in his heart.
He threw his head back and howled along.
Owooooo!
The animals looked at each other.
Hey, said the monkey.
I know that sound.
That's no special king, said the elephant.
That's just a jackal!
He's been fooling us, roared the lion.
Chandu got a fright.
He jumped up and ran away as fast as he could.
Out of the forest, and he never came back.
After a few weeks the blue dye came off.
Then Chandu was an ordinary jackal again.
And do you know what?
That was actually much nicer.
He could go back and live with his family.
They howled at the moon together.
And he didn't have to be afraid anymore that someone would find out his secret.
The lesson of this story: don't pretend to be someone else.
You are good just the way you are.
And whoever lies gets found out in the end.
The end.
